text:
infra-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: P99 request latency above configured SLO in eu-west-1. Detected 00:03:12 ago. Threshold=1200ms, current p99=3872ms. Impacted routes: /v1/generate (streaming).

maya (oncall): paging in. seeing the alert on my phone. I'm looking at the router dashboards.

pagerduty: Incident triggered: high-latency-eu-west-1. Pager assigned to maya. Severity: SEV2.

maya (oncall): quick summary — p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 3.8s for streaming endpoints in eu-west-1, tail spikes correlate with higher queue depth on router pods and sustained connection stalls in stream shard 7.

sanjay: I'm on infra. I see a sudden increase in requests pinned to a small subset of gateway hosts — one host in az-a has ~45% of traffic for shard 7. That looks like a routing weight skew.

jenna: adding early customer impact: support reports several customers in EU complaining about slow streaming tokens and incomplete streams. Emily, do you have tickets?

emily-support: ticket #C-11234 and #C-11235 show repeated reconnects and missing streaming chunks, starting ~08:12 UTC.

ricky-ml: ML infra note — Model KV cache hit rate hasn't changed, but we see many long-lived KV fetch waits (100-200ms) during the spike. Could be backpressure from router hot partitioning.

ops-sre: I pulled router logs, snippet: 
```
2026-03-14T08:13:02Z router[gw-az-a-07]: route_select: policy=weighted-shard, shard=7, chosen_host=gw-az-a-07, host_queue_depth=72
2026-03-14T08:13:03Z router[gw-az-a-07]: stall: stream_wait=1200ms, conn_wait=340ms, kv_wait=180ms
2026-03-14T08:13:05Z router[gw-az-a-07]: error: client_stream_timeout after 5s
```

maya (oncall): can we confirm whether the loadbalancer weights changed recently? Any config rollouts?

sanjay: Checking infra rollouts — no LB config deploys in the last 12h. However, the autoscaler had an anomaly: az-b pool had an autoscale cooldown and didn't add new gateway pods, while az-a kept scaling. That created an effective weight imbalance.

jenna: So combination of autoscaler cooldown + weighted routing amplifies requests to fewer gateways -> hot partition -> queue growth -> streaming stalls -> p99 spike. Makes sense.

maya (oncall): Immediate mitigation options — 1) force re-balance (set routing policy to round-robin), 2) manually adjust weights to shift traffic away from gw-az-a-07, 3) drain the hot gateway for new connections. Preferences?

ops-sre: My vote is #2 then #3. Quick weight adjust is fastest. I can run the command to lower az-a weight to 0.4 and increase az-b to 0.6 for shard 7.

ricky-ml: Also consider enabling fallback to smaller model variant for streaming on overloaded hosts to reduce per-token latency — but that's a mid-term tweak.

maya (oncall): go for the weight adjust. ops-sre, post the exact command you'll run. I'll annotate incident timeline and let support know.

ops-sre: running: 
```
# adjust routing weights for shard 7 in eu-west-1
rtrctl set-policy --env=prod --region=eu-west-1 --shard=7 --policy=weighted --weights az-a=0.4,az-b=0.6 --reason="incident 1859001234 emergency weight rebalance"
```

ops-sre: command executed. API returned 202 accepted. Propagating.

maya (oncall): seeing gradual drop in queue_depth on gw-az-a-07 from 72->18 over 40s, p99 trending down to ~1.6s. Good.

emily-support: telling customers that we're actively mitigating, ETA ~5-10min to stabilize.

pagerduty: Note: send follow-up notification to SEV2 after stabilization.

ops-sre: second mitigation: draining new connections from gw-az-a-07 to allow in-flight streams to finish and reduce tail. 

ops-sre: drain command: 
```
rtrctl drain-host --host=gw-az-a-07 --grace=120 --reason="incident mitigation"
```

ops-sre: drain in progress. Host now refusing new stream handoffs. Existing streams finishing.

maya (oncall): p99 down to 980ms now for streaming endpoints in eu-west-1. p95 stable around 380-450ms. Good sign.

ricky-ml: verifying downstream — model servers CPU and GPU utilization stayed normal. This confirms router-side hotspot is root cause.

jenna: logging immediate customer impact: 5 customers experienced token delays >2s, 2 had reconnects. No data loss reported. Marking potential SLA blips.

maya (oncall): creating incident timeline for postmortem. Assigning owners: RCA infra lead = sanjay, router code review = jenna, mitigation runbook update = ops-sre.

sanjay: early hypothesis: autoscaler cooldown + routing policy that persists weights during scale events caused effective weight skew. We need to adjust autoscaler to emit LB weight updates or have routing fallback to zone-aware round-robin during imbalance detection.

ops-sre: I'll open a runbook PR to add an automated weight-check step: if any host >30% of shard traffic for >60s, trigger auto-weight-balance.

maya (oncall): we should also add an alert for 'host share > X' so we can detect hot partitions before p99 breaches.

jenna: agreed. Also will add a test in CI that simulates an az cooldown and verifies routing re-balances.

emily-support: CS update sent — "stabilized, mitigation applied, follow-up postmortem forthcoming." Customers asked for timeline and RCA once available.

pagerduty: Incident status => mitigated. Monitor for 1 hour. If p99 stays <1s, we can declare resolved.

maya (oncall): handing off to sanjay for next-hour watch. I'll stay reachable if it flares. Sanjay, please take over pager.

sanjay: taking pager. I'll watch region metrics and ensure autoscaler cooldowns don't reoccur.

ops-sre: opening postmortem ticket: PM-5823. Initial notes in the ticket include timestamps, commands run, affected hosts, customer impact, and action items (autoscaler weight sync, alert).

maya (oncall): final note: add a short blameless note about why the weighted policy exists (cost/latency tradeoffs) and whether we should have an emergency 'balanced' toggle in console for quick manual switch.

ricky-ml: recommend also adding a model-facing graceful degradation path for streaming that'll kick in if router latency > threshold (reduce chunk size or switch to less aggressive compression). Not immediate, but a backlog item.

jenna: will draft the runbook PR and CI test. ops-sre, please link the PR in PM-5823.

emily-support: closing customer-facing update thread. Will reopen if customers report regressions.

maya (oncall): incident mitigated, handing off. Postmortem owners know their tasks. Closing Slack thread for live mitigation.

ops-sre: :white_check_mark: notes: mitigation timeline recorded, weights adjusted, host drained, p99 returned below target. Follow-ups assigned.
